input: User-pasted independent audit, external repository access failed
scope: Reconcile seven findings with existing registry/interventions/chart/media; verify selected original sources, not full review

checks.status: new safety references; existing adult comparator not new
checks.finding: StatPearls reports 35–45% systemic absorption of topical 2% hydroquinone; not an absorbed fetal dose. UKTIS v3 advises against use during pregnancy because reproductive data are limited; inadvertent exposure is not usually grounds for termination. LactMed distinguishes unstudied breastfeeding exposure from formal contraindication; some experts advise against prolonged use, avoid infant contact/ingestion. Avoid elective use pending individualized advice.
checks.rejected: Do not infer mercury exposure from hydroquinone itself; external mercury report not independently verified and contamination is formulation-specific. Do not use adult concentration/duration as pregnancy guidance.

checks.status: new primary trial and lactation reference
checks.finding: 44 adults randomized; 12 weeks; 0.5% bakuchiol twice daily versus 0.5% retinol once daily. Both improved photoaging outcomes; no significant between-group difference, retinol more scaling/stinging. Pregnancy and breastfeeding explicitly excluded. Not an equivalence or reproductive safety trial. Mechanism does not establish safety.
checks.safety: Bakuchiol research-only, not proven safe in pregnancy or lactation. Avoid topical retinoids in pregnancy; do not blanket-label all retinoids contraindicated in lactation. LactMed considers topical tretinoin low risk owing to poor absorption but no direct lactation study; avoid nipple/areola and infant skin contact. Oral retinoids require separate rules.

checks.status: existing guideline and review; N305 is publication-location alias of S064, retain both IDs for existing references; no new independent source
checks.finding: Canadian 2025 guideline: build toward ≥120 minutes moderate-to-vigorous activity/week across ≥4 days, aerobic and resistance, gradual symptom-based return. Encourage starting within 12 weeks where appropriate, not universal clearance or deadline. Daily PFMT with technique support; tailor for pain/overactivity. Sedentary ≤8h and recreational screens ≤3h conditional, very low certainty; sleep hygiene rather than strict sleep dose. Unstable BP >140/90 is a screening item, not emergency threshold or sole clinical rule. Wound, bleeding, dyspnea, chest pain, fainting and other symptoms require differentiated triage. No automated eligibility.
checks.numeric_notes: Beamish odds outcomes distinguish PFMT-only versus broader interventions; POP single trial, not severity or guaranteed prevention; IRD does not establish DRA resolution. Guideline and its companion review share evidence.

checks.finding: Third trimester total choline 930 vs 480 mg/day; 26 original completers, 21 re-recruited, 20 analyzed at age seven (11 vs 9). SAT means 0.71 vs 0.56, SE 0.04 each; difference 0.15 (95% CI .03–.27), p=.02. Overall hit percentage main effect not significant (84 vs 76%, p=.12); specific vigilance interaction reported separately. Not IQ, not absolute probability of improved child cognition.
checks.limitations: Small cohort, attrition, multiple outcomes, replication required; mixed public/commercial funding. 450 mg/day pregnancy and 550 mg/day lactation are total-intake AIs, not supplement doses; no routine 930 mg recommendation.

checks.status: both publications already registered; expand existing extraction
checks.finding: S028 T028 70 participants, 6–12 months postpartum, 12 weeks. Existing O002 (IRD +1 mm, CI −1 to +4) and O003 (strength +9 Nm, CI 3–16) retained, new thickness +0.7 mm (CI .1–1.3). R009 Benjamin review MD −.43 cm (CI −.82 to −.05), six trials n161 moderate certainty. Do not infer early postpartum readiness, severe DRA safety or mandatory avoidance of curl-ups. Doming may prompt individualized modification, not validated standalone contraindication.
checks.overlap: Review estimates are not independent trials; exact cohort crosswalk pending.

checks.finding: 2370 couples seeking infertility treatment; male 5 mg folic acid+30 mg elemental zinc daily vs placebo for six months. Live births 404/1185 vs 416/1185, adjusted/reported RD −0.9 percentage points (95% CI −4.7 to 2.8); DNA fragmentation +2.4 pp (CI .5–4.4), 29.7 vs 27.2. GI events more frequent. 1629 semen samples at six months, 1773 visits, complete live birth follow-up.
checks.limitations: Does not apply to treatment of deficiencies, all supplements or maternal periconception folic acid; not healthy male population. Do not recommend tested high doses or infer causality beyond tested combination and population.
